observations.text: SP, on the first exposure to the formation approach as wingman, held the landing configuration but did not stabilize the observance angle during the turn to final, which opened beyond 55 degrees. Lateral separation exceeded the +20 feet allowance from the 10-foot reference point and the IP directed the closure and flew part of the approach. Performance remains at the desired level for this Training Section; marginal, with independent application of the fingertip criteria expected to improve over the next sorties.

SP kept the wingman position in landing configuration into the flight area and completed the straight-in approach with the IP's verbal advice only, without any intervention on the controls. Lateral separation was contained at the +20 feet limit from the 10-foot reference point and vertical separation stayed within +10 / -5 feet of the Leader's wing level. Corrections to the observance angle were recognized with some delay but were applied by the SP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP kept the wingman position in landing configuration through the instrument approach with No1 maneuvering up to 30 degrees of bank. Deviations were minor, with lateral separation reaching 25 feet against the 10-foot reference point and the observance angle opening to about 40 degrees, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Vertical separation remained inside +10 / -5 feet of the Leader's wing level. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the formation approach in landing configuration with accuracy and speed, applying the fingertip criteria without any prompting. Lateral separation was held within +10 feet of the 10-foot reference point, the observance angle within 30 degrees plus or minus 5 degrees, and vertical separation within +10 / -5 feet of the Leader's wing level throughout the turn to final. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the formation approach in landing configuration with exceptional precision, anticipating the Leader's power reductions and bank changes up to 30 degrees. Lateral separation, vertical separation and observance angle showed negligible deviations from the fingertip criteria, the wingman position remaining essentially fixed from the flight area to the straight-in segment. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a power-lead technique that lagged the Leader's throttle changes, did not maintain the wingman position in landing configuration during the turn to final. Lateral separation opened past the +20 feet allowance from the 10-foot reference point and the observance angle exceeded 55 degrees, with the result that the IP directed the rejoin and flew part of the approach.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, divided attention between the landing checks and the wing position and did not keep the observance angle within the fingertip criteria. The position degraded to more than +20 feet of lateral separation from the 10-foot reference point and more than 10 feet above the Leader's wing level, with the result that the IP took control and re-established the wingman position.

SP maintained the wingman position in landing configuration and completed the formation approach within the standards required for this Training Section, using the IP's verbal advice on the closure. Lateral separation reached the +20 feet limit from the 10-foot reference point and the observance angle settled at 50 degrees plus or minus 5 degrees, the corrections being recognized and applied with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier recognition of the opening lateral separation is expected to improve.

SP kept the wingman position in landing configuration into the flight area and through the straight-in segment without the IP's intervention. Minor deviations occurred, with lateral separation reaching 25 feet against the 10-foot reference point and the observance angle opening to about 40 degrees, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Vertical separation remained within +10 / -5 feet of the Leader's wing level. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP applied the fingertip criteria accurately and quickly throughout the formation approach, holding the landing configuration and the wingman position with No1 maneuvering up to 30 degrees of bank. Lateral separation remained within +10 feet of the 10-foot reference point, the observance angle within 30 degrees plus or minus 5 degrees and vertical separation within +10 / -5 feet of the Leader's wing level, with no prompting from the IP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the formation approach with exceptional precision, matching the Leader's configuration and power changes so that corrections were anticipated rather than reactive. Deviations in lateral separation, vertical separation and observance angle were negligible from entry into the flight area to the straight-in segment. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a visual cross-check confined to the Leader's fuselage instead of the full fingertip references, did not maintain the observance angle during the descending turn to final. The angle opened beyond 55 degrees and lateral separation exceeded the +20 feet allowance from the 10-foot reference point, with the result that the IP directed the corrections and flew part of the approach in landing configuration.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with the landing configuration, the approach clearance and the wing position handled simultaneously, did not keep the vertical separation referenced to the Leader's wing level. The aircraft climbed more than 10 feet above the Leader's wing level and lateral separation opened past the +20 feet allowance from the 10-foot reference point, with the result that the IP intervened on the controls to restore the wingman position.

SP, due to late and oversized bank corrections during the Leader's 30-degree turn, did not hold the lateral separation within the fingertip criteria. Separation reached the +20 feet limit from the 10-foot reference point and the observance angle stabilized at 50 degrees plus or minus 5 degrees, with the result that the wingman position was restored only after the IP's verbal prompts, recognition and correction being delayed.

SP, due to situational awareness limited to the runway environment rather than to the Leader's wing line, did not maintain the observance angle in landing configuration on the straight-in approach. The angle opened to 50 degrees plus or minus 5 degrees and lateral separation reached the +20 feet limit from the 10-foot reference point, with the result that the corrections were applied only after the IP's verbal prompts and with delay.

SP kept the wingman position in landing configuration within the standards required for this Training Section, without the IP's intervention. Lateral separation twice reached 25 feet against the 10-foot reference point and the observance angle opened to about 40 degrees, deviations that were recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter control of the lateral separation inside +10 feet is expected to improve with further formation exposure.

SP flew the formation approach with accuracy and speed, applying the fingertip criteria throughout the instrument approach and the straight-in segment. Lateral separation was held within +10 feet of the 10-foot reference point, the observance angle within 30 degrees plus or minus 5 degrees, and vertical separation within +10 / -5 feet of the Leader's wing level, with no prompting from the IP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the formation approach in landing configuration with exceptional precision, anticipating the Leader's bank changes up to 30 degrees and the power reductions on final. Lateral separation, vertical separation and the observance angle showed negligible deviations from the fingertip criteria for the whole approach, and the wingman position required no visible correction. Above end of block MIF achieved.
